title: The Cider Press Batches
story: Come October, Felix wheels the old cider press out of the boatyard's paint shed and lends it to the neighbors for a fair share of each batch. This year four pressed, Felix included, each with a different apple mix and a hand-drawn label for the jugs. Nobody wrote down the gallons, and a fair share needs numbers. Who pressed which mix, who drew which label, and how much cider did each one make?

texts: The neighbor with the owl label made more cider than the neighbor with the moon label.
Of the neighbor who made 5 gallons and the neighbor who made 10 gallons, one pressed a wild mix and the other pressed a tart mix.
Of the neighbor with the tart mix and the neighbor with the spicy mix, one made 5 gallons of cider and the other made 15 gallons of cider.
Cyrus made more cider than Felix.
The neighbor with the star label made exactly 5 gallons more than the neighbor with the spicy mix.
Marta made less cider than the neighbor with the moon label.
Felix made exactly 5 gallons more than the neighbor with the moon label.
